title: Acquire Reaction Event Laws
status: Completed normal rendered answer; no scientific validation by dispatcher

answer.html:
A constructive advance: acquire the reaction-event law directly

I developed a way to acquire certified reaction-event predictions from a compact rule program without first constructing a closed Markov description of every relevant molecular configuration.

The construction applies to a specific, checkable class: locally evolving molecular modules coupled through a finite collection of reaction gates. Within that class, it provides:

  • The distribution of when the next selected reaction occurs and which reaction it is.
  • A numerical certificate for that entire distribution, including the possibility of no reaction before a deadline.
  • Composition across repeated reactions, known resets and substrate depletion.
  • A separate operation for predicting extremely rare reaction times without integrating across their enormous waiting-time horizon.

I implemented the central case and obtained a certified calculation for 80 binary sites, representing 280≈1.21×10242^{80}\approx1.21\times10^{24}280≈1.21×1024 configurations. I also obtained a rationally certified rare-event calculation on the same configuration scale.

The underlying renewal identities have substantial prior art. Finite-strength reaction sinks and gated-reaction laws have long been expressed through unperturbed propagators and return probabilities. The contribution to pursue here is the complete route from compact rules to an executable, certified and reusable scientific operation, together with its precise applicability conditions—not a claim to have discovered renewal theory. arxiv.org+1

All calculations below are new work from this continuation. I have not treated the preceding conversation’s 64-system tests, 125,055 comparisons or chemotaxis dimension claim as established evidence.

1. The representation that makes this possible

Consider a molecular system whose internal configuration is

x=(x1,…,xn),xℓ∈Eℓ.x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n),\qquad x_\ell\in E_\ell.x=(x1​,…,xn​),xℓ​∈Eℓ​.

A module can be a single site or a small collection of interacting sites. Between selected reaction events, suppose the generator decomposes as

Q=⨁ℓ=1nQℓ.Q=\bigoplus_{\ell=1}^{n}Q_\ell.Q=ℓ=1⨁n​Qℓ​.

Thus the unmarked dynamics evolve independently across modules.

Now introduce mmm marked reactions. Reaction jjj fires at rate κj\kappa_jκj​ when the relevant internal configuration equals

aj=(aj1,…,ajn).a_j=(a_{j1},\ldots,a_{jn}).aj​=(aj1​,…,ajn​).

The full configuration space has size

∏ℓ=1n∣Eℓ∣,\prod_{\ell=1}^{n}|E_\ell|,ℓ=1∏n​∣Eℓ​∣,

but the rule program can specify the local dynamics and each aja_jaj​ in a much shorter representation.

What must actually be obtained from the source

The decomposition cannot simply be assumed because the input looks modular. A compiler needs to establish it.

For the restricted rule grammar I implemented, the acquisition procedure is:

  1. Inspect each unmarked rule’s guards and updates. Connect variables that the same rule reads or changes.
  2. Form the resulting components. Build the local generator inside each component.
  3. Check the marked guards. Each must specify a finite list of complete configurations on the relevant components.
  4. Check initialization and resets. Their distributions must be supplied as products or finite positive mixtures of products.

The numerical kernel in the new implementation is constructed from the acquired local generators and the gate specification. It is not supplied separately as an unexplained formula.

There are two substantive boundaries.

First, a component can itself be too large to enumerate. This procedure avoids the global product expansion; it does not make an arbitrarily complicated local component inexpensive.

Second, a short wildcard guard does not automatically give a small reaction interface. A guard that leaves many relevant variables unspecified may represent exponentially many reactive configurations. The prototype rejects such a guard when the required finite interface has not been established.

An important distinction makes the construction stronger than an independence approximation:

The free dynamics factor across modules. The distribution conditioned on “no reaction yet” generally does not.

The method retains the correlations created by survival conditioning through a memory kernel.

and the matrix kernel

Let fj(t)f_j(t)fj​(t) be the density that the first marked reaction occurs at time ttt and has mark jjj. Then

Why the equation is exact

Follow the free process, with the selected reaction clocks attached but without applying their resets. Decompose its occupation at a gate according to:

  • no marked reaction having occurred yet; or
  • the first marked reaction having occurred at gate iii, at some time s<ts<ts<t.

In the second case, the configuration at that instant is known: it is aia_iai​. The subsequent free transition probability to aja_jaj​ is the product appearing in Kij(t−s)K_{ij}(t-s)Kij​(t−s).

Multiplying the occupation identity at aja_jaj​ by κj\kappa_jκj​ gives the equation.

The actual post-reaction reset does not enter this first-event equation. It enters when the resulting operation is composed with the next one.

For binary modules, evaluating K(t)K(t)K(t) takes O(m2n)O(m^2n)O(m2n) local-factor work. There is no sum over 2n2^n2n configurations. Solving the integral equation still costs time and memory determined by the horizon, requested accuracy and kernel behaviour; a small kernel matrix alone does not guarantee uniformly cheap numerical evaluation.

A generic stability estimate for an integral equation can introduce a very pessimistic factor growing exponentially with reaction rate times horizon. The probabilistic inverse above avoids that factor.

It does not eliminate the need to resolve a sharp kernel or to bound numerical integration and rounding errors.

also has reduced denominator degree 2n2^n2n.

Therefore:

Every exact finite autonomous linear realization of this density requires at least 2n dimensions.\boxed{ \text{Every exact finite autonomous linear realization of this density requires at least }2^n\text{ dimensions.} }Every exact finite autonomous linear realization of this density requires at least 2n dimensions.​

An exact homogeneous phase-type realization likewise needs at least 2n2^n2n transient states.

Yet evaluating its compact return kernel still needs only nnn factors.

This separation need not rely on enormous waiting times

Choose the rational family

λi=1+2−i,pi=1−1n,n≥2.\lambda_i=1+2^{-i}, \qquad p_i=1-\frac1n, \qquad n\ge2.λi​=1+2−i,pi​=1−n1​,n≥2.

The subset sums are distinct: the integer part identifies subset cardinality, and the binary fractional part identifies membership. All local relaxation rates remain in (1,1.5](1,1.5](1,1.5].

Eaτ=1κ(1−1/n)n,\mathbb E_a\tau = \frac{1}{\kappa(1-1/n)^n},Ea​τ=κ(1−1/n)n1​,

so

eκ≤Eaτ≤4κ.\frac e\kappa \le \mathbb E_a\tau \le \frac4\kappa.κe​≤Ea​τ≤κ4​.

The exponential exact-realization requirement thus occurs on an ordinary reaction timescale.

The lower bound has a precise scope. It concerns finite, constant-coefficient linear probability evolution and homogeneous phase-type representations. It does not exclude compact age-dependent programs, symbolic kernels, nonlinear descriptions or network-free simulation. It also does not establish that an approximate Markov representation must be large.

Its role is to show why insisting on a small exact closed state can discard a tractable scientific query.

9. Position relative to existing work and the remaining scientific boundary

The literature materially constrains the novelty claim.

Pre-expansion observable acquisition is already an active capability. The October 2026 MolFoundry work derives auxiliary observables and finite event models directly from graph rules, under explicit counting and jump-construction conditions. Its scope directly rules out a broad claim that “rules plus queries can produce executable observable dynamics” is itself new. 
arxiv.org
+1

Exact stochastic reduction is also established. Species-equivalence methods compute maximal reductions within their stated species-sum class. The earlier Astra rational-linear construction addresses a different observation class, but that distinction must remain precise. 
arxiv.org

Certified exit distributions are established too. ETFSP, for example, supplies computable total-variation bounds through state-space truncation. The operation developed here obtains its inputs and certificate through compact local propagators and a finite reaction interface. 
arxiv.org

The candidate contribution is therefore narrower and more concrete:

Acquire an event-prediction operation directly from compact rules, certify its complete output law through a probabilistic residual, and compose it across scientifically specified resets and phases—even when exact finite linear state prediction requires exponentially many dimensions.

The special factor-one residual bound, its obtaining procedure and the complete compositional implementation warrant further comparison with the closest numerical renewal methods. I do not yet have a defensible historical-priority claim for the complete construction.

The strongest next scientific extension is partially specified or overlapping reaction gates with compact, certified entrance information. A full-configuration gate tells us the hidden state at an event. A wildcard gate generally leaves a distribution whose correlations matter to the next reaction. Extending the operation requires a representation of that information, or a controlled approximation to it; a low-rank expression for the hazard alone does not supply one.

That is now a sharper frontier: the present construction already handles timing, turnover noise, depletion and rare waiting laws. The next representation must preserve enough information at broader reaction interfaces to carry those capabilities into less restrictive molecular rule families.
